pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITIONS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why do you enjoy reading stories?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify the parts of a narrative composition
2. write coherently on different topics
3. create a narrative composition for self-expression

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions

Teach
• Focus skill: identify the parts of a narrative composition.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do you enjoy reading stories?
2. How do you make your composition interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
